newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PLESSEY SELLS UNIT TO OMEGA .
newsitem.headline: PLESSEY SELLS UNIT TO OMEGA .

text.p: South Africa's Plessey Corp Ltd announced on Tuesday it had sold its consumer electronics division to Omega Holdings Ltd for 75 million rand.
The 75 million rand is payable in cash by June 30 and was based on the net asset value of the unit concerned, Plessey chief executive John Temple said in a statement.
The figure excluded certain additional amounts such as work in progress and goods in transit, which would be paid for against delivery.

The announcement follows close on the heels of last month's agreement for Omega to acquire the Plessey operations relating to the marketing, selling amd servicing of Telefunken and Pioneer television and audio products in South Africa.
Plessey's consumer electronics division made a pre-tax loss of 35 million rand for the year to March 31, Temple said.
Temple said the transaction would have no effect on the net asset value per share of PLessey.
Proceeds from the sale would boost working capital for Plessey's communications and professional electronics units.

"Shedding the consumer electronics operations will allow us to increase management focus on growing exports and developing global operations in communications and professional electronics," Temple said.
